input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The exception-message predicate requires the regular expression to match the entire exception message.
- failure path: Given an exception message with a matching prefix followed by additional diagnostic text, the retry condition returns false and Tenacity propagates the exception without retrying.

Reviewer finding
- description: The regex check was changed from `match.match(...)` to `match.fullmatch(...)`. The commit title only announces accepting an empty message, so this is an unrelated behavior change.
- rationale: Trigger: `retry_if_exception_message(match="foo")` with an exception whose text is "foo bar". Before, `re.match` anchored only at the start and the retry happened. Now `fullmatch` requires the whole string to match, so no retry happens. Existing users relying on prefix matching silently stop retrying.
critique: The finding points to the switch to fullmatch, which requires the regex to match the entire exception message. It gives the same failure path: a message with a matching prefix plus extra text no longer triggers a retry. This is the same mechanism as the labeled defect.
